terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: The sheet is orthographic-like and is not used for pixel projection. Match each admitted elevation independently during review.

objectClass.notes: Four admitted elevations support a stylized exterior-only reconstruction; no interior geometry is inferred.

reasoning: The narrow tower, offset balcony, horned roof, lantern jib, and banner create a strongly interrupted asymmetric silhouette.
Repeated plank seams, shingles, iron plates, bolts, windows, and finials require grouped systems to stay inside the 4,400-triangle target.
Four admitted views resolve the exterior depth, but their generated ornamental cadence varies slightly, so front and hero views control identity.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Macro tower masses, meso service assemblies, and grouped micro construction details all survive at the elevated gameplay camera.

resolvedUncertainties: Generated views disagree on minor horn and rope placement; use the front and hero horn silhouette, with the rear view controlling rope anchors.
Shingle, bolt, and stone counts are cadence evidence rather than literal counts; use grouped repetition under the 5,600-triangle hard ceiling.
Lantern interior, doorway interior, and balcony room interior remain closed or emissive-backed exterior surfaces.

detailInventory.note: Twelve observed details are mapped to implemented component local features or material local overrides.

details.description: Green moss concentrates in the lowest irregular foundation joints and post bases.
details.affects: stone albedo, roughness, and cavity response

details.description: Chunky damp-stone courses use uneven widths rather than a uniform brick grid.
Tall vertical plank rhythm is framed by dark posts and cross rails on every elevation.
Diagonal timber braces interrupt the tall wall panels and reinforce the balcony.
Square iron corner plates and raised bolt heads repeat at beams, posts, and door rails.
details.affects: metal construction rhythm and edge highlights

details.description: Overlapping oxidized teal shingle rows step down both steep roof slopes.
details.affects: roof row relief and teal value variation

details.description: Paired dark horn forms flare outward from the upper eaves with metal collar bands.
Small amber arched windows carry dark vertical and horizontal mullions.
details.affects: window material separation and facade scale

details.description: The hanging amber lantern is enclosed by a tapered iron cage and short chain.
details.affects: lantern negative space and emissive containment

details.description: Warm amber core remains contained inside the iron lantern cage.
A round iron door pull and pointed post caps anchor the service entrance.
The blank teal banner ends in an uneven torn lower edge without an emblem.

anatomy.note: Architectural object; character anatomy does not apply.

definitionOfDone: A floor-seated 7.8 by 10.5 by 7 yard exterior shell reads immediately as the horned Fenwarden tower from four gameplay-relevant angles, retains a clear service stair and balcony, and remains within the 4,400-triangle target and 5,600 hard ceiling.

qualityCriteria: The stone base stays broad and low while the timber tower remains narrow and vertically dominant.
failureModes: tower reads as a generic square house
foundation consumes too much of the height

featureGroups.name: Steep teal roof and upturned horn silhouette
qualityCriteria: Steep roof slopes, central finial, and paired horn arcs remain legible from front and hero views.
failureModes: horns float away from eave collars

featureGroups.name: Entry, balcony, lantern, and banner asymmetry
qualityCriteria: The accessible front stair is balanced by offset balcony, lantern jib, and blank teal banner without blocking the apron.
failureModes: service stair or balcony has no readable negative space

featureGroups.name: Timber, iron, stone, and shingle construction rhythm
qualityCriteria: Grouped plank seams, diagonal braces, metal plates, bolts, stone courses, and shingles read without one mesh per mark.
failureModes: uniform detail density exceeds the triangle budget

featureGroups.name: Contained amber window and lantern hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Amber shapes stay behind dark mullions and cage bars, subordinate to the roof silhouette.

visualDeltaChecks: tower height to foundation width and roof height ratio
horn span and roof peak silhouette against front and hero evidence
entry stair, balcony, lantern, banner, and rear rope placement
plank, shingle, stone, metal-plate, and mullion cadence
warm emissive containment and teal roof value separation
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not model an explorable or visible interior.
Do not replace horn arcs, balcony negative space, or stair profile with painted details.
Every inventoried mark must resolve to a named component feature or material override.
Use grouped or instanced repetition for shingles, bolts, windows, and finials.
Keep +Z as the front and preserve the unobstructed service apron.

mustMatch: entry, balcony, lantern, banner, and rear-rope service cues
amber windows contained by dark frames

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Steep teal roof with paired horn arcs
Accessible front door, hood, and stair
Offset balcony, lantern, banner, and rear rope
Amber windows and lantern contained by dark frames
Timber brace, shingle, stone, and fastener cadence
Moss and rain-darkening stay at contact zones

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: Generated turnaround pixels contain baked studio lighting, so they guide palette and finish only; shared independent normal and roughness maps provide runtime response.

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

acceptance: Silhouette reads correctly without materials.
Quality contract has named all required macro feature groups before code generation.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Build the component hierarchy implied by the pre-spec complexity assessment.
acceptance: Macro, meso, and repeated structures meet qualityContract.minimumSpecDepth.
Parent-child relations, joints, seams, sockets, and contact points are explicit.
Every attached child appendage/connector has parentSocket, localStart/localEnd, contactType, embedDepth or overlap, and gapTolerance.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Refine shape, deformation, bevels, tapers, curves, asymmetry, and visible local geometry.
acceptance: Important visible forms are represented in component geometryDescriptor, deformations, localFeatures, or repetitionSystems.
Endpoint-based child parts are rooted at their attachment sockets and do not visibly float away from parents.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Match material color, roughness, bump, and local variation.
acceptance: Reference-derived albedo palette records dominant, secondary, and accent colors per visible material.
Each important material defines roughness variation and at least one normal/bump/displacement response.
Local material overrides, dirt/wear/stains/moss/chips/scratches or equivalent masks are tied to evidenceRefs.
Thin, transparent, reflective, wet, or fibrous materials document alpha/transmission/clearcoat/metalness/fiber response when relevant.
Generated preview uses procedural albedo/roughness/bump texture or vertex color variation instead of one flat color.
Generated preview uses independent PBR maps at 1024px or higher for the quality-first tier.
If source pixels are available, referencePbr extraction passed at confidence >= 0.7 or the pass is stopped/requesting better references.
Macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands are visible at the intended review distance without obvious tiling.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Add procedural surface locality such as normal/bump/displacement, AO, dirt, stains, chips, grain, moss, scratches, and wear.
acceptance: Every required material feature group has local overrides or surfaceDetail tied to evidenceRefs.
A grazing-angle close-up proves that normal/height detail breaks highlights naturally and does not read as smooth plastic.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make material and form readable under neutral turntable lighting plus optional reference lighting.
acceptance: lightingFromPhoto identifies key light direction/color/intensity, fill light, rim or environment light, and ambient color.
Exposure, tone mapping, background color/gradient, shadow softness, and contact shadow behavior are specified.
Lighting does not hide geometry/material gaps and screenshots can be compared fairly to the reference.
Neutral, grazing, and reference-matched lighting checks distinguish material errors from lighting errors.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make the model ready for future animation, transformation, physics, or destruction.
acceptance: Macro and movable meso components have stable pivot nodes.
Sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata are present for future runtime actions.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance after visual fidelity is accepted.
acceptance: Triangle count, draw calls, instancing, LOD strategy, and FPS target are documented or verified.
Repeated detail is instanced or simplified where possible without breaking silhouette/material believability.

lodPlan.strategy: full two-material merged shipping geometry with all silhouette and service cues
same GLB; renderer tier may shed nonblocking emissive and shared surface maps, never collision-bearing silhouette

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Group shingle, fastener, stone, and plank cadence before removing any identity-critical silhouette or service cue.

lightingFromPhoto: Neutral cool-white key from upper front-left separates roof planes without baking light into vertex color.
Broad low-intensity fill lifts the deep timber facade while preserving iron and plank seams.
Soft neutral rim/environment light outlines horns, balcony, banner, and roof peak; ACES-like tone mapping at exposure 1.
Neutral gray background and soft contact shadow prove floor seating; a grazing pass checks shingle and metal relief.
proceduralStrategy: Block the exact plinth, tower, and roof proportions in world-yard space with +Z front.
Add entry stair, open balcony, horn arcs, lantern jib, banner, window frames, and rear rope as named exterior systems.
Represent plank, shingle, stone, and fastener cadence with grouped geometry and semantic vertex colors.
Use shared independent normal and roughness support maps at runtime; never project baked studio lighting.
Merge semantic buckets only in the shared finalizer and preserve all authored socket metadata.
animationAnchors: root pivot node supports whole-object translation, rotation, scale, and visibility changes
component pivot groups support later local transforms without rebuilding geometry
destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
risks: Warden crops are below 1k pixels on the narrow dimension, so fine bolt and shingle counts are cadence approximations.
Generated views vary minor horn and rope placements; the explicit front/hero/rear precedence prevents contradictory geometry.
The blockout pass still needs browser render and comparison evidence before the img2threejs structural pass unlocks.
